title: Tie-breaker Signal Matrix and Heuristics for LLM Output Quality Observability
body:
Purpose

This is a working note proposing a compact, operator-friendly signal matrix and a set of deterministic heuristics (tie-breakers) that observability systems should use to decide automated actions and surface high-confidence quality regressions for LLM inference. Goal is to reduce noisy alerts, make fallback decisions more explainable, and provide small dashboard widgets that help SREs and ML engineers triage quality-related incidents quickly.

Context and motivation
- We have many possible signals for output quality: token-level latency and truncation, model confidence proxies, reranker scores, classifier flags (toxicity/PII), eval set regressions, customer feedback events, and sampled human labels. Individually they are noisy.
- During rollouts or traffic surges we want deterministic, auditable tie-breakers so that fallback rules, A/B rollbacks, and alerting thresholds behave predictably.
- This doc outlines a signal matrix, priority ordering, sampling strategy for expensive signals, and concrete dashboard/trace anchors to support investigations.

Signal matrix (short names and intent)
- perplexity_proxy: cheap per-request score from last-token logits dispersion; correlates with model uncertainty when prompt length stable.
- rerank_conf: score from reranker returned when pipeline enabled; strong indicator of candidate quality.
- safety_flag: binary/enum from automated safety classifier (toxicity, phi, etc.).
- semantic_diff: approximate embedding distance between user prompt and response canonicalization; catches hallucination drift in specific datasets.
- eval_realtime: rolling pop of golden prompt set inference and evaluation; expensive but high signal-to-noise.
- human_report: customer feedback or bug-report tagging; low recall but high precision.
- latency_tail: p95/p99 token generation time; sometimes correlates with partial outputs or truncation errors.

Priority ordering rationale (for tie-breaking)
1) safety_flag: safety incidents should always short-circuit and trigger immediate mitigation (rate-limit, fallback to safe-model, or quarantine route).
2) eval_realtime + human_report: paired high-trust signals; if either shows regression beyond configured delta, escalate to oncall and auto-fallback to previous model snapshot for traffic above threshold.
3) rerank_conf: if rerank_conf drops below configured percentile while other signals normal, prefer temporary canary throttle and increased sampling for eval_realtime.
4) semantic_diff + perplexity_proxy: used together; high perplexity with above-threshold semantic_diff raises suspicion. Alone they cause increased sampling, not immediate rollback.
5) latency_tail: used primarily for operational SLOs; escalates to infra routing and capacity change rather than model rollback unless paired with quality regressions.

Deterministic tie-breaker examples
- Example A (safety first): safety_flag == true -> immediate alert severity P0, route traffic to safety-fallback model, create trace anchor containing request id and classifier trace.
- Example B (eval confirms): eval_realtime shows absolute drop in BLEU-like score > 6% and human_report rate doubles in 30m -> auto canary rollback and page oncall.
- Example C (noisy proxies): perplexity_proxy spikes 40% but rerank_conf and eval_realtime stable -> do increased sampling of eval_realtime for next 2k requests, create dashboard annotation but no rollback.

Sampling strategy for expensive signals
- Always sample 100% for safety_flag (cheap classification).
- Eval_realtime: baseline 1% of traffic; raise to 5-10% when any proxy crosses soft threshold. Keep a FIFO reservoir so samples are uniformly distributed across tenants and routes.
- Human_report: stream events to a short-lived staging table and join to traces for 24h; do not persist raw free text beyond retention policy.
- Semantic_diff: compute for 10% of requests by default and scale up on proxy triggers.

Dashboard and trace design notes
- Tiny widgets for operator console (no heavy SQL):
  - "Tie-breaker Summary" compact row per route: recent safety_count, eval_delta (30m), rerank_p50, perplexity_p95, human_reports_24h, action_state (none/canary/rollback). Color-coded.
  - "Sampling Heatmap" showing percent of traffic sampled for eval_realtime per tenant over time. Helps spot blindspots where we sampled too little.
  - "Recent Safety Traces" list: links to traces with classifier decision path and classifier logits.
- Trace anchors: every sampled request should attach these tags: route, model_version, sample_type (eval/semantic/audit), safety_decision, rerank_score. Use these anchors for fast session reconstruction.

Alerting heuristics and runbook snippets
- Soft alerts (notify channel only, no page): perplexity_proxy p95 > baseline*1.5 across 30m AND rerank_conf p50 drop > 10% -> add eval sampling and create ticket.
- Hard alerts (page SRE): safety_flag true count > 3 in 10m OR eval_realtime stat delta > configured absolute threshold -> page oncall, mark route as degraded in console, start rollback window.
- Runbook: when paged, operator should 1) verify trace sample, 2) check recent eval_realtime examples, 3) evaluate traffic split and initiate rollback toggle if eval delta confirmed. Attach checklist link in alert.

Privacy and data retention notes
- Safety classifier inputs and sampled texts should be redacted for PHI where flagged; do not store raw user text beyond 7 days for eval samples unless explicitly approved.
- Linked artifacts include GH issue for safe-fallback implementation and linear task for eval pipeline scaling.

Open questions and follow-ups
- How to standardize semantic_diff threshold across different prompt intents? Need small taxonomy by route (qa, chat, rerank, summarization).
- How to expose tie-breaker decisions to customers for transparency without leaking internal heuristics?
- Implementation work: small telemetry shim in runtime to emit sample markers and a dashboard microwidget. Estimate 2 sprints.

Next steps (practical)
- Sync with applied-ml to pick a default eval_realtime golden set for chat and summarization by 2025-03-10.
- Prototype the 1-row Tie-breaker Summary widget in dashboard sandbox this sprint.
- Add small e2e test covering safety short-circuit behavior and ensure trace anchors propagate through canary routing.

Notes to self
- Keep heuristics simple and explainable. Operators prefer deterministic thresholds over fuzzy ML thresholds for triage.
- Save a few annotated example traces to CONFLUENCE-1234 for onboarding.
